diagrams: ok — 2 SVG figures (SR latch with table; latch vs flip-flop timing diagram from the real VCD): role=img, title, desc and caption present; only sv-* classes; meaning carried by labels, dashes and line weight, not colour; labels match the text; caption tags updated to D6 slide headings

findings: F1-16-jargon: SR latch "made of two cross-coupled NOR (or NAND) gates" with S setting Q = 1 → "two cross-coupled gates (NOR gates in this chapter)"; a NAND latch has active-low inputs, as the lab extension says (D6 "SR Latch"; R1)

F1-16-jargon: Metastability "caused by ... or by S and R released together" → caused for example by an input changing too close to the sampling instant; the S = R = 1 case moved to an unverified note (D6 "Metastability")

F1-16-layer2: "In a real circuit the two gates are never exactly equal ... That is metastability" → a bistable loop has a balanced in-between state where it can linger for an unpredictable time; the S = R = 1 case is flagged as unverified (D6 "Bistable Circuit", "Metastability")
F1-16-layer3: "Latch-based designs exist, but they are a specialist technique" → the textbook avoids latches ("We don't use latches in this text") and warns of accidental ones (D7 "Latch")
F1-16-layer3: "Simulators also start every stored value as x" → Icarus Verilog, the simulator used, starts stored values as x, as the runs show (R1, R2)

F1-16-hardware: "Many chips build their storage elements from cross-coupled inverters plus switches that open and close with the clock" → the slides call cross-coupled inverters the fundamental building block of state elements (D6 "Bistable Circuit")

F1-16-breaks: metastable output: "logic reading it may see 0 in one place and 1 in another" → output between the valid levels for an undetermined time, neither a clean 0 nor a clean 1 (D6 "Metastability")
Not verified box: Layer 3 box: real setup/hold/clock-to-Q times and metastability probabilities (part-specific; no data sheet); and that a real NOR latch released from S = R = 1 goes metastable.

Not found: Whether a real NOR SR latch released from S = R = 1 goes metastable (searched D6 Metastability, Bistable Circuit; D2 §3.1): not stated → unverified box in Layer 3; the chapter reasons it from D6.
Not found: Setup, hold, clock-to-Q and metastability numbers of a named part: no data sheet used → unverified box, no numbers.
Not found: That latch-based design is "a specialist technique" (D6, D7): not stated → replaced by D7's statement that the textbook does not use latches.

Not found: That a 1-bit Verilog signal has exactly four values and storage starts as x (IEEE 1364 text not opened): D7 names the values 0, 1, x, z; the x start is shown for Icarus Verilog by runs R1, R2 and stated as this simulator's behaviour.
Not found: Clock-driven switches inside storage elements and flip-flops at pipeline-stage boundaries (D6, D2): not stated in the opened material → removed / reworded as a forward reference to HW202.
Not found: Petzold's "Code" (D3): not opened (web budget) → its single tag removed; D6 covers the SR latch.
